tower-of-hanoi.title: Move largest disk first if not on target
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the largest remaining disk is not already on its goal peg and there are no smaller disks on top of it, move it directly to its goal peg. This reduces the problem size and avoids unnecessary moves of smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest free disk is not yet on its destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a smaller disk before the largest free disk, causing extra moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve subproblem after moving largest disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After placing the largest disk on its goal peg, treat the remaining n‑1 disks as a new Tower of Hanoi subproblem with the same rules. Solve that subproblem before proceeding further.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after the largest free disk has been moved to its goal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Continuing to move disks without resetting the subproblem, leading to misordered moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive move sequence for k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use the classic recursive algorithm: move k‑1 disks from source to auxiliary, move the kth disk to target, then move k‑1 disks from auxiliary to target. This guarantees a legal sequence that respects size constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to transfer a stack of k disks from one peg to another.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disks in a non‑recursive order that violates the size constraints.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as final parseable output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the last parseable list of moves in the response is the complete solution, because the verifier reads only the final list of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When formatting the answer, put the move list at the very end of the response.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including the move list earlier in the text, causing the verifier to miss it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, mentally simulate each move from the initial state to ensure the final configuration matches the goal. This catches mistakes before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the answer, run through the entire move sequence mentally or on paper.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves some disks on the wrong peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Concise final move list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep the reasoning brief and place only the complete move list as the final element of the response. Extra text after the list can prevent the parser from reading the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the answer, avoid any trailing commentary after the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to stop reading moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When adding a move, check that the disk being moved is currently the topmost disk on its source peg and that it is not placed onto a smaller disk. This prevents illegal moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move list, before committing each move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative smallest-disk cyclic algorithm
tower-of-hanoi.principle: For any Tower of Hanoi problem, repeatedly move the smallest disk to the next peg in a fixed direction (clockwise or counter‑clockwise), alternating with the only other legal move. This yields a correct solution for the classic all‑on‑one‑peg start.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When solving the classic Tower of Hanoi where all disks start on a single peg and the goal is to move them to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Using a non‑cyclic approach for the classic problem, resulting in suboptimal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk must be moved onto a peg that currently contains a smaller disk (or a stack of smaller disks), first relocate those smaller disks to a free peg. This allows the larger disk to be placed at the bottom of the target peg without violating size rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the target peg for a larger disk is occupied by a smaller disk that blocks placement of the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk onto a peg that already has a smaller disk, violating the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget to include the move list or assume the answer is implicit.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a non‑empty list of moves as the final parseable output.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may run out of tokens or stop early, omitting later moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the entire move sequence is included and verify that the final configuration matches the goal before submitting.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of the current stack state while constructing moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before adding a move, check that the disk is the topmost on its source peg and that the move respects size constraints.
